stated.value: Existing NIR pilot on one powder formulation; a different API and excipient blend is being introduced
Would like to reuse the existing calibration

status_reason: Material, target (API concentration) and location (tablet press feed frame) are known, so a provisional assessment is possible; reuse of the old calibration is not approved and Raman cannot be assumed to rescue it.
answer: The old NIR calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend, and adding Raman does not preserve it either: a NIR + Raman model is a new fused model that needs its own calibration and validation. The first test is NIR + Raman in the feed frame on the new blend, with NIR alone as the baseline on the same validation samples.

inline.headline: Test NIR + Raman in the tablet press feed frame on the new blend, with NIR alone as the baseline
inline.probe: Combined NIR reflection and 785 nm Raman fiber probe in a compact shaft; NIR diffuse reflection probe for the baseline
inline.install: Inserted directly into the tablet press feed frame
inline.fiber: Silica Vis-NIR (350-2400 nm) with Al/Cu-coated silica for the Raman path
inline.test_against: NIR alone (diffuse reflection) on the same validation samples
inline.not_final_because: The new blend has no validated calibration yet, excipient fluorescence is unknown, and the Raman gain is reported only in one cited feed-frame study.

problems.text: The existing NIR calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend; it is a chemometric model built and validated for one matrix, so it must be re-tested and most likely replaced.

Adding Raman does not keep the old calibration valid: a fused NIR + Raman model is built on newly fused data and needs its own calibration and validation on the new formulation, and whether fusion helps is a hypothesis.
Raman signals are weak and can be masked by much stronger fluorescence from many organic compounds, so the new API and excipients must be checked for fluorescence before Raman is committed to.
NIR diffuse reflection suits powder at 0.5-1 mm depth, but whether the pilot probe geometry still samples the new blend in the same way must be confirmed.

methods.why: Online method that suits powders and works with remote fiber probes, but it needs a new chemometric calibration on the new blend.
The same quantity (blend potency in a tablet press feed frame) was measured with combined NIR reflection and 785 nm Raman probes; the two methods carry complementary information.

methods.method: Raman (785 nm excitation; Raman shift axis in cm-1)
methods.why: Adds molecular backbone and non-polar group information, but its signal is weak and can be masked by fluorescence.
Mid-IR is limited to very thin layers and ATR suits liquids and soft solids, not powder in the feed frame.

questions.q: What API concentration range and accuracy must the new blend's potency measurement meet?
questions.why: This sets the go/no-go criteria and shows whether NIR alone may be enough.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory method will give the reference API concentrations for the calibration and validation samples?
questions.why: Reference values must come from independent analyses, not from the instrument's own calibration.

questions.q: What are the API and each excipient, and do you have their pure-component spectra or fluorescence behaviour?
questions.why: Needed to identify key spectral features and to check whether excipients will mask the Raman signal.

questions.q: Which probe and geometry does the existing pilot use in the feed frame, and is there room for a combined probe shaft?
questions.why: Determines whether the same spot can be measured with both methods and whether the sampling is unchanged.

experiment.objective: Test whether the existing NIR calibration transfers to the new blend, and whether adding Raman on the same spot improves API prediction over NIR alone.
steps: Prepare calibration and validation blends of the new API and excipient blend across the potency range, and record pure-component spectra of the API and each excipient.
Measure every sample in the feed frame with the NIR reflection probe and the combined NIR + Raman (785 nm) probe, on the same spot and time-synchronised.
Obtain independent laboratory reference API concentrations for every sample.
Predict the new blend with the old NIR calibration to confirm the premise, then build and validate NIR-only and fused NIR + Raman PLS models on separate validation samples.
Compare the NIR-only and fused models on the same validation data; if Raman gives no gain, use NIR alone and check Raman fluorescence before concluding.
references: De Man, A, et al. (2024). Evaluating the improvement of blend potency measurements in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press using combined NIR and Raman spectroscopy. Analytical Chemistry, 96(26), 10586-10593.
experiment.go_no_go: Acceptance criteria to be set by the client before testing; the fused model must beat the NIR-only model on the same validation data.

pathway.key_features: NIR bands from hydrogen bonds and polar groups and Raman bands from the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, to be identified from pure-component spectra.
pathway.path_reason: Key spectral features and a valid calibration for the new blend are not yet known; the AFS pathway starts with a multi-method lab test on the customer process.

multispectral.why: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman provides the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so the information is complementary.
multispectral.test: Compare NIR-only and fused NIR + Raman models on the same independent validation samples against laboratory reference values; accept the combination only if it beats NIR alone.

assumptions: The existing pilot uses a NIR reflection probe in the feed frame.
The powder blend is heterogeneous, so both methods must see the same small area.
No reference data, concentration range or accuracy target was provided.
The excipients and API of the new blend have not yet been characterised spectroscopically.
